clue.text: Change the last bit of clothing in struggle to dress

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the word for struggle, cutting it open

parts.note: to strain is to struggle or strive hard

indicators.note: the final letter of the word clothing is taken
to change these letters is to rearrange them into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wrestles with the last item of clothing while trying to get dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram makes GHTE, from the three-letter word plus G. 'Dress' is the military sense, as in dressing ranks, not putting on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress a line of soldiers is to align it, making it neat and even.

clue.text: A bit of body language

definitions.meaning: a part of the body, the muscular organ in the mouth
a ... is a language, as in one's mother ...

explanation.definitionFit: The organ of the mouth also names a spoken language, as in a foreign tongue.

clue.text: The devil of an election process, over there

parts.note: a poll is the process of voting in an election
yon is an old word meaning that place over there

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the faraway election is a devilish business.
explanation.walkthrough: The name comes from the Book of Revelation and is used by Bunyan in The Pilgrim's Progress for the fiend Christian fights.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollyon, the destroyer, is a biblical name for Satan, the prince of hell.

clue.text: Hurry, as Penelope had to?

definitions.meaning: to get a move on, a British colloquial phrase for hurrying up
Penelope, wife of Odysseus, had to keep at her loom weaving a shroud to stall her suitors

explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom for 'get busy, hurry up' is read literally of Penelope in Homer's Odyssey, who wove by day and unpicked by night.
explanation.definitionFit: The British colloquialism means to start moving briskly, to make haste.

clue.text: Little creature, a morsel to perch?

parts.note: a tad is a small amount, a morsel
a pole is an old measure of length also called a perch or rod

explanation.surface: A tiny animal gets a small bite of food on its way to its roost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perch' looks like a bird's roost or a fish, but here it is the old British unit of length, also called a rod or pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A young frog or toad in its larval stage is a small water creature.

clue.text: New prayer for part of church

parts.note: an Ave (Ave Maria) is a prayer to the Virgin Mary

explanation.surface: A newly composed prayer is to be said in one area of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The central body of a church where the congregation sits is its main section.

clue.text: Apply, in standard English, for fighter's body

indicators.note: the word for apply sits inside the word for standard

parts.note: a standard is a flag or banner
to use something is to apply it

explanation.surface: A soldier seems to be told to use standard English when talking about a boxer's physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighter' suggests a boxer, but it is a fighter plane, whose main body is the fuselage.
explanation.definitionFit: The main body of an aircraft, which holds crew and payload, is its central structure.

clue.text: English writer who was initially Greek, briefly

definitions.text: English writer who was initially Greek, briefly

parts.words: English writer who was initially Greek, briefly
parts.note: the writer's initials were G K, which is also the short form of the word Greek

explanation.walkthrough: G. K. Chesterton was known by his initials, and 'Gk' is the standard abbreviation of Greek; 'initially' means 'by initials'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert Keith Chesterton, creator of Father Brown, was an English author known by his initials G.K.

clue.text: Swear on Bible purse has no money

parts.note: AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible

indicators.note: the word for money is taken away from the word for purse

parts.note: a pouch is a small bag or purse
P stands for penny or pence, British money

explanation.surface: Someone vows on the Bible that their purse is empty.
explanation.definitionFit: To avouch is an old verb meaning to affirm or vow solemnly.

clue.text: Will not become involved in nude review — it's not customary

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, getting tangled up in it
to review is to look over again, so these letters are revised into a new order

parts.note: wont is a contraction of will not, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to take part in a naked revue, saying it is not the done thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram gives UNED, which is cut open by the contraction. The surface suggests a theatrical revue.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwonted means unusual, out of the ordinary, the opposite of habitual.

clue.text: The House of Commons is unrivalled

definitions.meaning: the lower chamber has no lords sitting in it, being without nobles

explanation.walkthrough: The Commons has no members of the peerage, who sit in the Lords, so it is cryptically without peers.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no equal or match means being without rival.

clue.text: Women's group very acceptable to Muslim ruler

indicators.note: the ruler takes in, or accepts, the abbreviation for very

parts.note: a bey was a governor in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: A group of women is said to find great favour with a sultan-like ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a company, traditionally used of girls or ladies, as in a bevy of beauties.

clue.text: Man is on notice he should stick at his task

definitions.text: Man is on notice he should stick at his task

parts.words: Man is on notice he should stick at his task
parts.note: reads as a warning to a worker, but describes someone whose job is pasting up notices

explanation.walkthrough: 'On notice' and 'stick at' seem to mean being warned to persevere; literally the man works on notices and sticks them up.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who pastes advertisements on walls and hoardings is a sign-sticker by trade.

clue.text: Very popular gal with leather that's kinky

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl in leather is quite the thing, though some think it rather kinky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's kinky' scrambles GAL and LEATHER together.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something fashionable, in vogue with everyone.

clue.text: Commotion as shell lands on a bear in the jungle

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece lands on top of the next, placing it first

parts.note: a hull is a husk or shell, as of a seed or ship
Baloo is the bear in Kipling's The Jungle Book

explanation.surface: A shell crashes down on a bear in the jungle, causing an uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: A hullabaloo is a noisy fuss or uproar.

clue.text: Being up late after telling stories is wearing

parts.note: telling stories is a euphemism for telling lies
if you are in a garment you are wearing it

explanation.surface: Staying up late after spinning yarns is tiring.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR inserted a stray LA; the page has none. 'Wearing' looks like 'tiring' but means IN. 'Being up late' is read as rising late, staying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying in bed past the usual hour in the morning means rising late.

clue.text: Devotee — one joining party subsequently

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a do is a party or celebration
later means afterwards, subsequently

explanation.surface: A fan joins the celebration only some time afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater is a worshipper of idols, hence an ardent admirer.

clue.text: Merciful old Pope

definitions.meaning: The name taken by fourteen popes

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means lenient; as a name it was taken by several early and medieval popes.

clue.text: Let diamonds, for example, fall into the wrong hands?

definitions.text: Let diamonds, for example, fall into the wrong hands?

parts.words: Let diamonds, for example, fall into the wrong hands?
parts.note: reads like jewels being stolen, but describes cards of a suit going to the wrong players

explanation.walkthrough: Diamonds suggest jewels and thieves; here they are a card suit, and the hands are card hands.
explanation.definitionFit: To have given out cards wrongly is to have made an error in dealing.

clue.text: Fully occupy quarters with well over a hundred

parts.note: E and N are compass points, also called quarters
a gross is 144, a dozen dozen

explanation.surface: Accommodation is filled up with well over a hundred guests.
explanation.definitionFit: To engross is to absorb someone's whole attention or occupy completely.

clue.text: Artificial intelligence?

parts.note: reads as computing, but means information that is deliberately slanted or manufactured

explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' is news or information, as in military intelligence; made-up information is spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Biased information spread to promote a cause is in effect fabricated news.

clue.text: Sleeps around to maximum extent

indicators.note: turned around, so the word for sleeps is read backwards

parts.note: naps are short sleeps

explanation.surface: Someone dozes off all over the place to the greatest possible degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is the full reach or extent of something, as in a wingspan.

clue.text: Sound, for example —- an expanse of water

indicators.note: the clue's opening word says the next letters are to be spoken

parts.note: EG is a standard abbreviation for for example; taken as written

explanation.surface: A sound, for instance, is a stretch of sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'e.g. an' gives 'ee-jee-an'. 'Sound' looks like a sea inlet, the false definition; it is the signal to say the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aegean is the sea between Greece and Turkey, a large body of salt water.

clue.text: Foolishly cares woman's a good looker

indicators.note: acting foolishly, the letters are jumbled into a silly order

parts.note: her is the possessive used of a woman

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly thinks a woman is good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolishly' turns CARES into SEARC. 'Good looker' suggests a beauty but means one who looks hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A searcher is someone who seeks thoroughly, a diligent hunter.

clue.text: Firm was cheating, director at last admitted

indicators.note: the final letter is let into the word for was cheating

parts.note: had means tricked or cheated, as in you've been had

indicators.note: only the final letter of director is used

explanation.surface: A company was swindling, and its director eventually confessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' takes R from director; 'admitted' puts it inside HAD, informal for cheated.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard means solid or unyielding.

clue.text: Material for wrapping comic opera's one record in

indicators.note: the record is placed inside the jumbled letters
comic suggests a funny, mixed-up version, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s is no letter
I is the Roman numeral for one
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A comic opera's single record needs some wrapping material.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram gives OIAPER, which the record splits after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilpaper is paper treated with oil to make it waterproof, used for packaging.

clue.text: One said to be leaving city

indicators.note: this signals the spoken form of the next word

parts.note: one who is leaving is an exiter

explanation.surface: A person is rumoured to be quitting the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One ... leaving' is a person who exits, an 'exiter'; said aloud it gives the Devon city.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is the cathedral city and county town of Devon in south-west England.

clue.text: Bad feeling about temporary home put on record

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
on means about, concerning
a tent is a portable shelter used as a temporary home

explanation.surface: Ill will arises about a temporary dwelling, officially recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: Discontent is dissatisfaction or unrest.
